title: UBIB upward-breaking concept, level-ice model tests (Otaniemi ice tank, 1:25), resistance at full scale, 1.0 m level ice

ship.name: UBIB concept hull (upward-breaking bow), Salmi (2014) test model
ship.source: Salmi (2014) section 4.3: L=4.0 m, B_max=0.4 m, T=0.3 m at lambda=1:25

convention_notes.bow_angle_deg: V15 bow: the thesis calls the alternative bow 'A10 deg entrance angle'; the V bow is the 15 deg entrance angle variant, used as phi in R_break
convention_notes.flare_deg: ASSUMPTION A2 -- the source does not tabulate the plating angle from the horizontal. 75 deg (15 deg from vertical, consistent with a 'V15' wedge) is used; the benchmark sweeps 60/70/75/80 deg and reports the band, because tan(alpha) drives R_crush
convention_notes.ice_belt_breath_m: narrow ice belt; the benchmark repeats the adjudication with B = 5.5 m to bracket hull-width uncertainty

facility.name: Aalto University Otaniemi ice tank
facility.model_ice: 40 mm model ice (target full-scale bending strength 500 kPa)
facility.test_program: level ice, towed/self-propelled runs at 3/6/9/12 knot equivalent speed

digitisation.method: verbatim transcription of the archived repository text extraction of Tables 5/8
independent_paths: pass A: column-major read, MN and knots kept, converted after transcription
pass B: row-major read, MN->kN and knots->m/s converted inline
checks: double_entry agreement over canonical + raw fields

uncertainty.definition: the source reports single values per run; run-to-run scatter and model-ice variability are described qualitatively but not quantified

applicability.role: external-validity probe: shows what the downward-bending closure family does when it is applied outside its breaking-mode envelope
limitations: concept hull (UBIB), not a ship in service; results are the author's channel-corrected values
plating angle (flare) not tabulated: ASSUMPTION A2 = 75 deg, swept 60-80 deg
narrow ice belt (5.5 m of 10 m breadth): hull-width convention swept
no measured ice compressive strength / elastic modulus: module defaults used

provenance.citation: Salmi, K. (2014) Alternative hull type for icebreaking vessels. MSc thesis, Aalto University School of Engineering, 3 June 2014
provenance.retrieval_note: Repository text-extraction bitstream retrieved HTTP 200 on 2026-11-10 from the worktree (aaltodoc DSpace 7 REST); the tables used are quoted verbatim into source/ so the digest is checkable offline. Captions precede table bodies in the extraction, which is why the 8-row block is attributed to Table 5 and the 4-row block to Table 8.

sources.role: verbatim quotation of Tables 5/6/7/8 from the open-access thesis

limitations: a single concept hull, tested in one campaign: it cannot separate ice-strength from geometry effects
measured resistance is post-processed by the author (channel friction replaced by theory)
upward-breaking mode: outside the Lindqvist-family envelope by construction

literature_baselines_kN._note: published UBIB theory (thesis Tables 6/7); context only, never truth

points.notes: R_alt_kN is Table 8 (additionally friction-corrected by the author, factors 1.5-2.46) -- kept as an alternative, never merged into R_meas
